title: Cipla Limited shows distinct growth shifts in US revenue measured in US dollars
abstract: This research note evaluates the financial performance and US revenue dynamics of Cipla Limited as of 16 October 2026. The main finding is that growth in US revenue measured in US dollars, on the same quarter a year earlier stood at 8.4 per cent in Q1 FY27, showing a clear break from earlier periods. We examined 8 quarters of filed results to understand these patterns across the pharmaceutical manufacturer listed on the National Stock Exchange of India. Revenue from operations reached Rs 6,142.0 crore in Q1 FY27, alongside an EBITDA margin of 25.0 per cent. Furthermore, we investigated multiple explanations regarding North America revenue growth while the lanreotide line stayed paused on a partner facility issue, alongside receivable days and India branded formulations revenue. The measure to watch going forward is growth in US revenue measured in US dollars, on the same quarter a year earlier in the next results as referenced in Table 4 and Figure 2.
introduction: Cipla Limited exhibits notable shifts in international revenue growth as documented in recent financial filings. This note focuses on growth in US revenue measured in US dollars, on the same quarter a year earlier, compared against 4 listed peers. As a pharmaceutical manufacturer listed on the National Stock Exchange of India, as of 16 October 2026, the company provides consistent disclosures that permit detailed quarterly examinations.
company_and_data: We examined 8 quarters of filed results to trace operational performance over time. Revenue from operations in Q1 FY27 was Rs 6,142.0 crore [1]. A year earlier, in Q1 FY26, it was Rs 5,467.0 crore. Additionally, the EBITDA margin was 25.0 per cent in Q1 FY27. Table 1 shows that revenue from operations rose from Rs 5,201.0 crore in Q2 FY25 to Rs 6,142.0 crore in Q1 FY27. Additional details appear in Table 2, Table 3, Table 4, Figure 1, Figure 2, and Figure 3.
findings: Growth in US revenue measured in US dollars, on the same quarter a year earlier stood at 8.4 per cent in Q1 FY27. Before Q3 FY26 it had averaged 3.5 per cent. The clearest break is in Q3 FY26, marking a notable upward shift in the quarterly trajectory as illustrated in Figure 2.
explanations: Cipla's North America revenue grew for three consecutive quarters while its lanreotide line stayed paused on a partner facility issue, a gap the company's own narrative does not separate out, which is supported and held against every check applied to its strongest rivals per Table 3. Receivable days grew faster than revenue over the last four quarters, suggesting channel stuffing ahead of a pricing change, though this explanation was weakened because the checks applied to it were not conclusive either way. India branded formulations revenue is substituting for US generics decline, which was rejected because the move is sector-wide, not company-specific.
outlook: The measure to watch is growth in US revenue measured in US dollars, on the same quarter a year earlier in the next results. Analysts and market observers will track whether the upward trend observed from Q3 FY26 onwards continues in subsequent filings across the peer group.
conclusion: The financial data demonstrates distinct operational changes for Cipla Limited across the examined periods. We conclude that monitoring international metrics remains essential for understanding the underlying drivers of revenue growth. Further disclosures will clarify the persistence of the trends identified in Q1 FY27.
